user.title: New flight search
user.description: Return trips every week: out on one day, back on another, within the hours you choose. Prices are for one adult. The [configuration guide]({guide_url}) explains every option, with examples.

data_description.name: For example Weekend from Milan.
data_description.origins: IATA codes, for example MXP and BGY. Each trip comes back to the airport it left from.
data_description.destinations: IATA codes of airports or cities (LON is every London airport). Leave empty to search anywhere: Ryanair only.
data_description.exclude_countries: Two-letter ISO codes, such as IT to leave out flights within Italy.
data_description.sources: Ryanair finds the cheapest fare to every destination with a few requests. Google Flights covers every airline, but only for a list of destinations and with many requests spread out over about an hour. Google Flights is read without an API: too many searches get your whole home connection a captcha from Google, so it is limited to {limit} requests a day.
data_description.google_origins: Only these of the departure airports are searched on Google Flights, for example the one not covered by Ryanair. Empty: all of them.
data_description.google_destinations: Searched only on Google Flights, so Ryanair can keep searching anywhere. Empty: the destinations above. Keep the list short: each one costs up to 2 requests per week and airport, and Google Flights is limited to {limit} requests a day.
data_description.weeks: How many weeks ahead, starting from the coming one.
data_description.direct_only: Google Flights only: Ryanair always flies direct.

summary.title: Google Flights requests
summary.description:
This search makes up to **{google_round} requests** to Google Flights a round, about {google_minutes} minutes, every {google_hours} hours: up to **{google_day} a day**, out of a limit of {limit}. It is the most it can make: the return is not searched when the outbound found nothing.

Ryanair, if chosen, makes one request per airport and week.

summary_high.title: Google Flights requests
summary_high.description:
This search makes up to **{google_round} requests** to Google Flights a round, about {google_minutes} minutes, every {google_hours} hours: up to **{google_day} a day**, out of a limit of {limit}. It is the most it can make: the return is not searched when the outbound found nothing.

Ryanair, if chosen, makes one request per airport and week.

⚠️ **Close to the limit.** Too many automatic searches get your whole home connection a captcha from Google. Unless you need them all, use fewer Google destinations, departure airports or weeks, or a longer interval.

app.title: Flight Prices app
app.description: The searches run in the Flight Prices app. On Home Assistant OS, install it from the app store ([how]({app_url})) and Home Assistant finds it by itself. With Docker, start its container and enter its address here.

data_description.password: Only if the app has one, set in its options or with FLIGHT_PRICES_PASSWORD.

hassio_confirm.description: The Flight Prices app is running. Set up a first search?

reconfigure.title: App address
reconfigure.description: Every search that uses this app moves to the new address.

data_description.password: Only if the app has one, set in its options or with FLIGHT_PRICES_PASSWORD.

init.title: Change the search
init.description: Changes apply at once: a source searches again only when what it searches has changed (more weeks included). The [configuration guide]({guide_url}) explains every option. This search now makes up to {google_day} Google Flights requests a day, out of a limit of {limit}.
